name: Daniella Pierson
milestone_by_age_26: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2020 at age 24 for building The Newsette into a newsletter with 500,000 subscribers and $40M revenue by age 25-26, making her one of the wealthiest self-made women of color in the US.
starting_point: Born in Jacksonville, Florida to a Colombian mother and American father; grew up in a middle-class household and attended Boston University.
current_position: Founder and CEO of The Newsette; co-founded Wondermind with Selena Gomez; Forbes later called her a cautionary tale for exaggerating professional claims.

trajectory.title: Idea for The Newsette conceived
trajectory.description: As a sophomore at Boston University, Pierson came up with the idea for a women-focused daily email newsletter after being unable to land a magazine internship.

trajectory.title: Launched The Newsette
trajectory.description: Sent the first edition of The Newsette on New Year's Day 2015 to eight subscribers, mostly family and friends, from her college dorm room.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Boston University
trajectory.description: Completed her degree at BU while growing The Newsette's subscriber base and honing her editorial style.

trajectory.title: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30
trajectory.description: Recognized by Forbes for building The Newsette into a newsletter with 500,000 subscribers and major brand sponsors including Ulta, Fidelity, and Bumble.

trajectory.title: The Newsette reached $40M revenue
trajectory.description: The company reported $40 million in revenue and was valued at $200 million, with Pierson dubbed the youngest wealthiest self-made BIPOC woman by Forbes.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Wondermind
trajectory.description: Launched mental fitness startup Wondermind alongside Selena Gomez and Mandy Teefey, valued at $100 million shortly after launch.

trajectory.title: Forbes published cautionary profile
trajectory.description: Forbes published a profile calling Pierson a cautionary tale of hubris, alleging she falsely claimed board membership and exaggerated professional achievements.

name: Samantha Shannon
milestone_by_age_26: Signed a six-figure book deal with Bloomsbury Publishing in 2012 at age 20 for The Bone Season series, and the debut novel became a New York Times bestseller upon publication in 2013 at age 21, with Shannon compared to J.K. Rowling.
starting_point: Born in Hammersmith, London in 1991 to an Irish-English family; grew up in Ruislip and began writing novels at age 15.
current_position: Award-winning New York Times and Sunday Times bestselling fantasy author; most recent book Among the Burning Flowers published in September 2025.

trajectory.title: Wrote first novel Aurora
trajectory.description: Completed her first novel Aurora at age 15, which was rejected by publishers but taught her foundational writing skills she later reused.

trajectory.title: Started drafting The Bone Season
trajectory.description: Began writing the first draft of The Bone Season between her first and second years studying English at Oxford University's St Anne's College.

trajectory.title: Signed six-figure Bloomsbury deal
trajectory.description: Signed a six-figure book deal with Bloomsbury Publishing for a seven-book series after the London Book Fair, with editor Alexandra Pringle championing the work.

trajectory.title: The Bone Season became NYT bestseller
trajectory.description: The Bone Season was published in August 2013 and became a New York Times and Sunday Times bestseller, with Shannon compared to J.K. Rowling.

trajectory.title: Published The Mime Order
trajectory.description: Released the second book in The Bone Season series, continuing the dystopian fantasy saga centered on dreamwalker Paige Mahoney.

trajectory.title: Published The Song Rising
trajectory.description: Released the third installment in The Bone Season series, solidifying her place as a leading voice in dystopian fantasy.

trajectory.title: Published The Priory of the Orange Tree
trajectory.description: Released her first standalone novel outside the series, which sold over a million copies in English worldwide.

trajectory.title: Published A Day of Fallen Night
trajectory.description: Released the prequel to The Priory of the Orange Tree, which became an instant #1 Sunday Times bestseller.

trajectory.title: Published Among the Burning Flowers
trajectory.description: Released her most recent novel in September 2025, continuing to build her reputation as a major fantasy author.

name: Gabe Fleisher
milestone_by_age_26: Built Wake Up to Politics into a daily political newsletter with approximately 50,000 subscribers by age 19, with readers including White House correspondents, MSNBC anchors, and members of Congress. He was profiled by the New York Times at 15 and has press credentials to cover Congress and White House events.
starting_point: Born November 8, 2001 in St. Louis, Missouri to Rabbi Randall Fleisher and sales director Amy Fleisher; grew up in University City, Missouri.
current_position: Founder and Editor-in-Chief of Wake Up To Politics on Substack with approximately 60,000 subscribers; graduated from Georgetown University in 2024.

trajectory.title: Interest in politics sparked
trajectory.description: The 2008 presidential election captured Fleisher's attention at age six, beginning a lifelong fascination with politics.

trajectory.title: Launched daily political newsletter
trajectory.description: Began writing The Daily Rundown email newsletter in April 2011 with his mother as the sole subscriber, from his middle school library.

trajectory.title: Newsletter reached 500 subscribers
trajectory.description: After being featured in the Clayton High School Globe and St. Louis Post-Dispatch, the newsletter grew to 500 subscribers.

trajectory.title: Profiled by New York Times
trajectory.description: The New York Times profiled Fleisher and his newsletter, causing subscriptions to skyrocket overnight and bringing national attention.

trajectory.title: Scooped de Blasio presidential run
trajectory.description: Became the first journalist to report that New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio would run for president in May 2019.

trajectory.title: Moved to Washington D.C. for college
trajectory.description: Began studying at Georgetown University, enabling on-the-ground reporting from the White House and U.S. Capitol Building.

trajectory.title: Newsletter surpassed 50,000 subscribers
trajectory.description: Wake Up To Politics reached over 50,000 subscribers including top politicians, media executives, and readers in all 50 states.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Georgetown and moved to Substack
trajectory.description: Graduated with a degree in government and journalism, and migrated the newsletter to Substack, reaching nearly 60,000 subscribers.

name: Maddy Thorson
milestone_by_age_26: Released TowerFall on Ouya in June 2013 at age 25, which became a cult hit and was expanded into TowerFall Ascension on PS4 in March 2014, also at age 25, receiving critical acclaim and establishing Thorson as a leading indie developer.
starting_point: Born March 18, 1988 in Canada; mother helped her acquire GameMaker at around age 14, sparking a lifelong game development career.
current_position: Director of R&D at Extremely OK Games (EXOK) in Vancouver, working on the upcoming game Earthblade.

trajectory.title: Started making games with GameMaker
trajectory.description: Thorson's mother helped her acquire a copy of GameMaker, connecting her to online forums and a community of aspiring game developers.

trajectory.title: Rebranded studio as Matt Makes Games
trajectory.description: After years of releasing free pay-what-you-want games including Jumper and FLaiL, rebranded her solo studio from Helix Games to Matt Makes Games.

trajectory.title: Began developing TowerFall
trajectory.description: Started prototyping TowerFall as a multiplayer archery combat game, initially nervous about pivoting from free to commercial game development.

trajectory.title: Released TowerFall on Ouya
trajectory.description: Released TowerFall in June 2013 on the Ouya console, where it became the standout game on the platform and a cult hit.

trajectory.title: Released TowerFall Ascension on PS4
trajectory.description: Expanded TowerFall into TowerFall Ascension for PS4 and PC in March 2014, receiving critical acclaim and establishing Thorson as a leading indie developer.

trajectory.title: Released Celeste to critical acclaim
trajectory.description: Released Celeste in January 2018, which became a cultural phenomenon and one of the most celebrated indie games of the decade.

trajectory.title: Reformed studio as Extremely OK Games
trajectory.description: Dissolved Maddy Makes Games and reformed the team as Extremely OK Games (EXOK) in Vancouver to begin work on Earthblade.

trajectory.title: Stepped back from public eye
trajectory.description: Took a step back from public visibility after a decade as an extremely visible figure in the indie game scene, focusing on development.

name: Rami Ismail
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Vlambeer in 2010 at age 21 and released Ridiculous Fishing in March 2013 at age 24, which won Apple Game of the Year and generated over $1 million in revenue within six months.
starting_point: Born October 30, 1988 in the Netherlands to an Egyptian father and Dutch mother; raised as a Muslim and attended the Utrecht School of the Arts.
current_position: Independent game industry advisor, mentor, and public speaker; runs gamedev.world and serves on the IGDA Board of Directors.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Vlambeer
trajectory.description: Dropped out of the Utrecht School of the Arts with Jan Willem Nijman to co-found Vlambeer after the school demanded rights to their game.

trajectory.title: Released Super Crate Box
trajectory.description: Vlambeer released Super Crate Box, a critically acclaimed arcade game that earned IGF recognition and established the studio's reputation.

trajectory.title: Ridiculous Fishing won Apple Game of the Year
trajectory.description: Released Ridiculous Fishing in March 2013, which won Apple's Game of the Year and generated over $1 million in revenue within six months.

trajectory.title: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30
trajectory.description: Featured with Jan Willem Nijman in Forbes 30 Under 30 for Games, recognizing Vlambeer's impact on indie game development.

trajectory.title: Won GDC Ambassador Award
trajectory.description: Received the Ambassador award from the Game Developers Choice Awards for activism encouraging diversity and supporting developers from less-developed countries.

trajectory.title: Vlambeer closed
trajectory.description: Announced the closure of Vlambeer, transitioning to advisory and mentorship roles in the global games industry.

trajectory.title: Founded gamedev.world
trajectory.description: Launched gamedev.world, a unique octolingual online games conference serving developers worldwide, as Executive Director.

name: Mike Bithell
milestone_by_age_26: Released Thomas Was Alone on June 30, 2012 at age 26, which sold over 1 million copies and won a BAFTA Games Award for Best Performer.
starting_point: Born November 7, 1985 in England; attended Newport university in Wales, one of the first game design courses in the country, before working as a junior designer at Blitz Games.
current_position: CEO and Creative Director of Bithell Games, which released TRON: Catalyst in 2025.

trajectory.title: Joined Blitz Games as junior designer
trajectory.description: Began working at Blitz Games on licensed titles including Tak and the Guardians of Gross and Dead to Rights: Retribution.

trajectory.title: Created Thomas Was Alone prototype
trajectory.description: Developed the initial prototype of Thomas Was Alone in 24 hours while at Blitz Games, releasing it free on Kongregate where it received 100,000 plays in the first week.

trajectory.title: Joined Bossa Studios
trajectory.description: Moved to Bossa Studios in February 2011, using the position to learn Unity and expand Thomas Was Alone into a full commercial title.

trajectory.title: Released Thomas Was Alone
trajectory.description: Released the full version of Thomas Was Alone on June 30, 2012, selling over 1 million copies and winning a BAFTA Games Award.

trajectory.title: Quit day job for full-time indie development
trajectory.description: On January 1, 2013, Thomas Was Alone passed the sales milestone that allowed Bithell to quit his day job and pursue independent game development full-time.

trajectory.title: Released Volume
trajectory.description: Released Volume, a sci-fi stealth game inspired by Robin Hood, featuring Andy Serkis as the villain.

trajectory.title: Released John Wick Hex
trajectory.description: Bithell Games released John Wick Hex, a strategy game based on the John Wick film franchise.

trajectory.title: Released TRON: Identity
trajectory.description: Released TRON: Identity, a choice-driven visual novel adventure for Disney, the studio's first licensed IP project.

trajectory.title: Released TRON: Catalyst
trajectory.description: Bithell Games launched TRON: Catalyst, building on the studio's growing portfolio of licensed narrative games.

name: Jan Willem Nijman
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Vlambeer in 2010 at age 20 and released Super Crate Box, which earned IGF recognition; later co-created Ridiculous Fishing (2013) at age 22-23, which won Apple Game of the Year.
starting_point: Born in the Netherlands; started using GameMaker at age 12 after reading about it in a children's computer magazine, making games throughout his youth.
current_position: Independent game designer and developer; co-creator of Minit, Disc Room, and Dustbiters; writes on Substack.

trajectory.title: Started making games with GameMaker
trajectory.description: Discovered GameMaker through a children's computer magazine and began creating games, starting by modifying the tutorial so the car sounded like a cow.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Vlambeer
trajectory.description: Dropped out of the Utrecht School of the Arts with Rami Ismail to co-found Vlambeer, refusing to give the school rights to their game.

trajectory.title: Released Super Crate Box
trajectory.description: Vlambeer released Super Crate Box, a critically acclaimed arcade game that earned IGF recognition and established the studio.

trajectory.title: Co-created Ridiculous Fishing
trajectory.description: Released Ridiculous Fishing, which won Apple's Game of the Year and generated over $1 million in revenue within six months.

trajectory.title: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30
trajectory.description: Featured alongside Rami Ismail in Forbes 30 Under 30 for Games, recognizing Vlambeer's impact on indie game development.

trajectory.title: Released Minit
trajectory.description: Released Minit, a minimalist adventure game where each life lasts only 60 seconds, co-developed with Kitty Calis and published by Devolver Digital.

trajectory.title: Vlambeer closed; released Disc Room
trajectory.description: Vlambeer officially closed, and Nijman released Disc Room, a sci-fi action game co-developed with Kitty Calis and JW Kuttlab.

name: Akshay Ruparelia
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Doorsteps.co.uk at age 17 and by age 19 the company was valued at £12 million, making him the UK's youngest millionaire.
starting_point: Born in Harrow, North East London to deaf parents who both worked two jobs; was a free school meal pupil and served as a young carer, motivating his entrepreneurial drive.
current_position: Founder and investor; stepped down as CEO of Doorsteps in April 2021; later founded AKR Growth, 1 Club, and Brdge AI.

trajectory.title: Founded Doorsteps.co.uk
trajectory.description: Launched Doorsteps.co.uk, an online estate agency charging £99 to sell a home with no commission, while still studying for A-levels.

trajectory.title: Raised £400,000 via Crowdcube
trajectory.description: Raised approximately £400,000 from around 500 investors via Crowdcube, valuing the company and making him the UK's youngest millionaire at 19.

trajectory.title: Company valued at £12 million
trajectory.description: Doorsteps was valued at £12 million after just over a year of operation, with Ruparelia selling his first house while doing his A-levels.

trajectory.title: Raised additional £1.5M in equity funding
trajectory.description: Raised over £1.5 million in total equity funding, growing the company to over 60 employees and selling over £1 billion worth of homes.

trajectory.title: Stepped down as CEO of Doorsteps
trajectory.description: Stepped down as CEO in April 2021 after growing Doorsteps to sell over £1 billion in homes across the UK in three years.

trajectory.title: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 Europe
trajectory.description: Featured on the Forbes 30 Under 30 Europe Technology list as the youngest honoree for disrupting the real estate market.

name: Vadym Melnyk
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Cervi Robotics (later Dronehub) at age 21 in 2015, and by age 23 secured a €200,000 European Space Agency contract, the genesis of Dronehub's autonomous drone infrastructure business.
starting_point: Born in 1994 in Ivano-Frankivsk, Ukraine; won a US State Department FLEX scholarship at 15 and moved to Poland at 18 with two words of Polish and a robotics habit.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Dronehub and VADYM.AI; based between Europe and the US (Research Triangle, NC); holds a US EB1A extraordinary ability green card.

trajectory.title: Moved to Poland
trajectory.description: Relocated from Ukraine to Poland at age 18 with minimal Polish language skills, settling in Rzeszow's Aviation Valley region.

trajectory.title: Founded Cervi Robotics
trajectory.description: Founded Cervi Robotics in Rzeszow, Poland, beginning development of autonomous drone technology for infrastructure inspection.

trajectory.title: Won European Space Agency contract
trajectory.description: Secured a €200,000 ESA contract for autonomous drone landing and battery swap technology, which became the foundation of Dronehub's business.

trajectory.title: Named to Forbes Poland 25 Under 25
trajectory.description: Recognized by Forbes Poland in their 25 Under 25 list, and rebranded Cervi Robotics to Dronehub to focus on the autonomous platform.

trajectory.title: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 Poland
trajectory.description: Featured in Forbes 30 Under 30 Poland for the second consecutive year, recognizing Dronehub's growth in the autonomous drone sector.

trajectory.title: Dronehub made Financial Times FT1000
trajectory.description: Dronehub was ranked on the Financial Times FT1000 list of Europe's fastest-growing companies, ranking #2 in Aerospace and Defense.

trajectory.title: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 Ukraine
trajectory.description: Featured in Forbes 30 Under 30 Ukraine, becoming a three-time Forbes honoree across Poland and Ukraine.

trajectory.title: Granted US EB1A extraordinary ability green card
trajectory.description: Awarded a US EB1A extraordinary ability green card, relocating operations partially to the Research Triangle in North Carolina.

name: Liu Yu
milestone_by_age_26: Became one of the youngest Executive Research Directors and General Managers of a Business Unit in SenseTime's history at age 26, managing a team of nearly 200 people with access to thousands of GPUs.
starting_point: Born in 1995 in China; studied at the Chinese University of Hong Kong where he earned a doctorate from the Multimedia Laboratory.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Vivix AI, an AI video generation startup valued at $1.32 billion within its first year.

trajectory.title: Won Microsoft Scholarship
trajectory.description: As a junior, won the only Microsoft Scholarship at his university and interned at the Visual Computing Group led by Professor Tang Xiao'ou.

trajectory.title: Joined SenseTime
trajectory.description: Joined SenseTime at the end of 2015, the company's second year, when the team had only dozens of people, contributing to the ImageNet World Championship.

trajectory.title: Completed PhD at CUHK
trajectory.description: Completed his doctorate at the Chinese University of Hong Kong while simultaneously working at SenseTime, flying between Beijing and Hong Kong weekly.

trajectory.title: Promoted to Executive Research Director
trajectory.description: Became one of the youngest Executive Research Directors and General Managers of a Business Unit in SenseTime's history, managing nearly 200 people.

trajectory.title: Led SenseMirage launch
trajectory.description: Led development of SenseMirage, an AIGC product that surpassed 3 million users within nine days of launch in September 2023.

trajectory.title: Left SenseTime to found Vivix
trajectory.description: Departure plans were revealed in October 2024, with investors including IDG Capital and HongShan immediately moving to back his new venture.

trajectory.title: Founded Vivix AI at $1.32B valuation
trajectory.description: Launched Vivix AI focused on real-time interactive video, reaching a $1.32 billion valuation within ten months of founding.

name: Jules Simiand Brocherie
milestone_by_age_26: Founded ExtraStudent which surpassed 100,000 users and secured €1.5 million in funding by May 2023, when he was 20 years old.
starting_point: Born December 1, 2002 in France; attended Lycee Notre-Dame-de-Sainte-Croix in Neuilly and briefly enrolled at IE University in Spain before leaving to focus on ExtraStudent.
current_position: CEO and Founder of ExtraStudent, an education and media group with approximately 300,000 users and 5 million monthly media views; Forbes and Vanity Fair 30 Under 30.

trajectory.title: Launched Eleves Solidaires during COVID
trajectory.description: Created a peer-to-peer educational support platform during the COVID-19 pandemic lockdown to combat school dropout, developing it in a single night.

trajectory.title: Founded ExtraStudent
trajectory.description: Renamed and relaunched the platform as ExtraStudent in January 2021, building it into a student mutual aid network across France.

trajectory.title: Named to Forbes France 30 Under 30
trajectory.description: Featured in Forbes France 30 Under 30 at age 19, with the platform reaching over 30,000 members across France.

trajectory.title: Surpassed 100,000 users and raised €1.5M
trajectory.description: ExtraStudent surpassed 100,000 users and secured €1.5 million in funding from investors including Benjamin Griveaux, Michael Benabou, Groupe M6, and Adrien Montfort.

trajectory.title: Partnered with Sciences Po Paris
trajectory.description: Announced a partnership with Sciences Po Paris, expanding ExtraStudent's reach into higher education orientation and guidance.

trajectory.title: Platform reached 300,000 users
trajectory.description: ExtraStudent grew to approximately 300,000 users with a media brand generating 5 million monthly views among a 13-24 year old audience.

name: Oliver Kent-Braham
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Marshmallow insurance in March 2017 at age 25 and raised a $1.2M seed round from Passion Capital and Investec Bank in February 2018 at age 26.
starting_point: Born to a British-Jamaican household; grew up with his identical twin brother Alexander, selling golf balls from a lake at age 12; attended Reed's School on a tennis scholarship and studied entrepreneurship at Bristol Business School.
current_position: Co-Founder and Co-CEO of Marshmallow, the UK's second Black-owned unicorn valued at $2B, with over 1 million drivers insured and 400-500 employees.

trajectory.title: Co-founded first venture Reel Money
trajectory.description: Co-founded Reel Money with his twin brother Alexander, an early entrepreneurial venture in the finance space.

trajectory.title: Joined Yoti as Growth and Partnerships
trajectory.description: Joined digital identity company Yoti, leading growth and partnerships and learning about scaling technology solutions.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Marshmallow insurance
trajectory.description: Co-founded Marshmallow with twin brother Alexander and David Goate in March 2017, building fairer car insurance for immigrants and newcomers to the UK.

trajectory.title: Raised $1.2M seed round
trajectory.description: Raised a $1.2 million seed round from Passion Capital and Investec Bank in February 2018 to grow the insurtech platform.

trajectory.title: Marshmallow reached unicorn status
trajectory.description: Marshmallow became the UK's second Black-owned unicorn, valued at $2 billion after a major funding round.

trajectory.title: Marshmallow insured over 1 million drivers
trajectory.description: Marshmallow grew to over 1 million insured drivers, 400-500 employees, and approximately $228.8M in total funding across 7 rounds.

name: Arnaud Delubac
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Greenly in October 2019 at age 24, and by age 26 in September 2021 the company raised a €2.5M seed round from Bpifrance and notable tech investors.
starting_point: Born in July 1995 in Paris, France; studied management at ESSEC Business School and engineering at CentraleSupelec, and worked in the French government on digital communication strategies.
current_position: Co-founder and CMO of Greenly, a climate tech company monitoring over 600M tons of CO2 for 3,500+ customers across 30+ countries; Forbes 30 Under 30 Europe.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Greenly
trajectory.description: Co-founded Greenly with brother-in-law Alexis Normand and Matthieu Vegreville in October 2019, initially as a personal carbon emissions tracking app.

trajectory.title: Raised €2.5M seed round
trajectory.description: Secured a €2.5 million seed round from Bpifrance and notable tech investors, pivoting from consumer app to B2B carbon accounting software.

trajectory.title: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 Europe
trajectory.description: Featured in Forbes 30 Under 30 Europe for building Greenly into a leading carbon management platform.

trajectory.title: Raised €21M Series A
trajectory.description: Greenly raised 21 million euros in a Series A round to expand its B2B carbon accounting platform across Europe.

trajectory.title: Raised €49M Series B
trajectory.description: Greenly raised 49 million euros in a Series B round led by Fidelity International Strategic Ventures, with participation from HSBC, HPE, and XAnge.

trajectory.title: Greenly reached 3,500+ customers
trajectory.description: Greenly grew to over 3,500 customers including LVMH, L'Oreal, and TripAdvisor, monitoring over 600 million tons of CO2 across 30+ countries.

name: Nikola Mrksic
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded PolyAI in 2017 at age 26, a London-based conversational AI company that raised $14.5M in total funding and was later valued at nearly $500M.
starting_point: Born and raised in Serbia; attended a Serbian maths high school and received a full scholarship to Cambridge University, where he studied computer science and mathematics and completed a PhD in machine learning.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of PolyAI, a Nvidia-backed conversational AI company with over $120M in VC funding, based in San Francisco.

trajectory.title: Joined VocalIQ as first employee
trajectory.description: Joined Cambridge spinout VocalIQ, a dialogue systems startup, as its first engineer while beginning his PhD under Professor Steve Young.

trajectory.title: VocalIQ acquired by Apple
trajectory.description: Apple acquired VocalIQ, and Mrksic worked with the Apple Siri team in Cambridge, gaining experience in large-scale conversational AI.

trajectory.title: Co-founded PolyAI
trajectory.description: Co-founded PolyAI with Tsung-Hsien Wen and Pei-Hao Su, fellow Cambridge researchers, to build enterprise-ready voice assistants.

trajectory.title: Raised initial funding
trajectory.description: PolyAI raised $14.5 million in total funding, establishing itself as a leading conversational AI company for enterprise customer service.

trajectory.title: PolyAI reached nearly $500M valuation
trajectory.description: PolyAI was valued at nearly $500 million, with its voice AI technology deployed across FTSE 100 companies.

trajectory.title: PolyAI backed by Nvidia
trajectory.description: PolyAI received backing from Nvidia and raised over $120 million in total VC funding, with inbound leads quadrupling after ChatGPT's release.

name: Dimitri Semenikhin
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Yacht Harbour in December 2014 at age 18 in Monaco, and by 2016 the platform was named by Investopedia as one of the 4 best platforms to find superyachts, with estimated revenue of $4.4M.
starting_point: Born December 15, 1996 in Moscow, Russia; moved to Monaco in 1999 with his parents Vladimir and Ekaterina Semenikhin; attended King's College London.
current_position: Founder of Central Jets and CEO of Seast; exited Yacht Harbour in 2020 after 8 years of operation.

trajectory.title: Founded Yacht Harbour in Monaco
trajectory.description: Founded Yacht Harbour in December 2014, coding the first prototype himself to create the world's largest superyacht database for sale and charter.

trajectory.title: Launched Brook AI interface
trajectory.description: Participated in the launch of Brook, a natural language processing interface for luxury yacht search, in November 2015.

trajectory.title: Named by Investopedia as top platform
trajectory.description: Yacht Harbour was named by Investopedia as one of the 4 best platforms to find superyachts, reaching over 5 million monthly impressions.

trajectory.title: Exited Yacht Harbour
trajectory.description: Exited Yacht Harbour in 2020 after growing it to the largest superyacht database with over 1,000 superyachts, $4.4M estimated annual revenue.

trajectory.title: Exited Yacht Harbour fully
trajectory.description: Fully departed Yacht Harbour by December 2022 after 8 years, transitioning to new ventures.

trajectory.title: Founded Central Jets and Seast
trajectory.description: Founded Central Jets, a private jet marketplace, and became CEO of Seast, continuing in the luxury transportation technology space.

name: Camila de Almeida Loures
milestone_by_age_26: Started on Vine and migrated to YouTube, reaching 16M+ subscribers by her mid-20s; published bestselling book 'Manual de Sobrevivencia do Adolescente' in 2016, signed with Universal Music in 2017, and was recognized as the largest female YouTuber in Latin America by age 26.
starting_point: Born February 7, 1995 in Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais, Brazil; father Geraldo Loures worked in luxury used car sales, providing a comfortable middle-class upbringing.
current_position: Brazilian YouTuber, singer, and digital influencer with over 16 million YouTube subscribers and 30 million Instagram followers; participated in A Fazenda 13 reality show in 2021.

trajectory.title: Viral breakthrough on Vine
trajectory.description: Gained fame on Vine by posting comedy videos, reaching 100,000 followers on the platform and establishing her digital presence.

trajectory.title: Launched YouTube channel
trajectory.description: Started her YouTube channel in May 2014, initially posting cooking, lifestyle, challenges, and music video parodies.

trajectory.title: Published bestselling book
trajectory.description: Published Manual de Sobrevivencia do Adolescente, which ranked among the best-selling books in the youth category in Brazil.

trajectory.title: Signed with Universal Music
trajectory.description: Signed a record deal with Universal Music, launching her music career and releasing multiple successful music videos.

trajectory.title: YouTube channel grew exponentially
trajectory.description: Channel growth accelerated with challenge vlogs, reaching millions of subscribers and billions of views.

trajectory.title: Reached YouTube Diamond Play Button
trajectory.description: Surpassed 10 million YouTube subscribers, earning the Diamond Play Button and becoming the largest female YouTuber in Latin America.

trajectory.title: Participated in A Fazenda 13
trajectory.description: Competed in A Fazenda 13, the Brazilian reality show equivalent to Big Brother, significantly expanding her mainstream entertainment visibility.

name: Whindersson Nunes Batista
milestone_by_age_26: Became the most-subscribed YouTube channel in Brazil from October 2016 to February 2018 at age 21-23, was the second most-subscribed channel globally behind PewDiePie in 2016, and was named Brazil's second most influential person, all before age 26.
starting_point: Born January 5, 1995 in Palmeira do Piaui, Piaui, Brazil; grew up in Bom Jesus in northeastern Brazil, producing comedy videos on a borrowed computer without professional infrastructure.
current_position: Brazilian YouTuber, comedian, actor, and boxer with 44.7 million YouTube subscribers; estimated net worth of $10 million; continues touring with stand-up comedy shows.

trajectory.title: Viral parody video breakthrough
trajectory.description: Posted the parody 'Alo vo, to reprovado' which received five million views within a week, launching his YouTube career.

trajectory.title: Channel hacked and rebuilt
trajectory.description: His YouTube channel was hacked and deleted, forcing him to start from scratch with a new account, rebuilding his audience.

trajectory.title: Became most-subscribed channel in Brazil
trajectory.description: From October 2016, his channel became the most-subscribed in Brazil and the second most-subscribed globally behind PewDiePie.

trajectory.title: Signed with BMG for music career
trajectory.description: Signed with music label BMG to launch his music career under the stage name Lil Whind, and starred in the film Os Parcas.

trajectory.title: Married Luiza Sonza
trajectory.description: Married singer Luiza Sonza in 2018 (they later divorced in 2020), during the peak of his YouTube dominance.

trajectory.title: Debut boxing fight
trajectory.description: Had his debut boxing fight against Mario Silva at New Champion 2 in Sao Paulo, winning and launching a boxing career.

trajectory.title: Competed in Kingpyn Boxing tournament
trajectory.description: Signed with Kingpyn Boxing and competed in the High Stakes Tournament, winning his fight against Filipek by TKO before losing in the semi-finals.

name: Gabriela Celeste Alaniz
milestone_by_age_26: Won the WBO world flyweight championship on June 18, 2022 at age 26, defeating champion Tamara DeMarco by corner stoppage, and later unified the WBA, WBC, WBO and The Ring flyweight titles.
starting_point: Born June 28, 1996 in Buenos Aires, Argentina; nicknamed 'La Chucky'; began her professional boxing career in 2018.
current_position: Professional boxer with a 15-2 record (6 KOs); former unified WBA, WBC, WBO and The Ring female flyweight champion; last fought in November 2024.

trajectory.title: Professional boxing debut
trajectory.description: Made her professional debut on May 25, 2018, defeating Maria Elizabeth Sanchez in Merlo, Buenos Aires, Argentina.

trajectory.title: Built early professional record
trajectory.description: Compiled a series of wins and losses in her first year, including victories over Daniela Gisele Molina and Romina Belen Gorosito.

trajectory.title: Won WBO Latino Flyweight title
trajectory.description: Captured the WBO Latino Flyweight title, establishing herself as a rising contender in the flyweight division.

trajectory.title: Won WBO World Flyweight championship
trajectory.description: Defeated champion Tamara DeMarco by corner stoppage on June 18, 2022 to win the WBO world flyweight championship.

trajectory.title: Lost to Marlen Esparza by majority decision
trajectory.description: Suffered her first loss via questionable majority decision to unified champion Marlen Esparza in July 2023 in San Antonio, Texas.

trajectory.title: Unified WBA, WBC, WBO and The Ring titles
trajectory.description: Won a split decision rematch against Marlen Esparza in April 2024 to claim the WBA, WBC, WBO and The Ring flyweight titles.

trajectory.title: Lost to Gabriela Fundora
trajectory.description: Lost by seventh-round TKO to Gabriela Fundora in November 2024, who became the youngest undisputed champion in boxing.

name: Evelyn Nazarena Bermudez
milestone_by_age_26: Won the IBF female junior flyweight world title on December 29, 2019 at age 23, added the WBO light-flyweight title in March 2022 at age 25, and became a unified IBF/WBO world champion before age 26.
starting_point: Born April 1, 1996 in Villa Gobernador Galvez, Santa Fe, Argentina; nicknamed 'La Princesita'; comes from a boxing family with three siblings who are also professional boxers.
current_position: Unified IBF, WBO and WBA female light-flyweight world champion with a 22-1-1 record (8 KOs); signed with Most Valuable Promotions.

trajectory.title: Professional boxing debut
trajectory.description: Made her professional debut on October 22, 2016, scoring a four-round unanimous decision victory over Adriana Maldonado in Rosario, Argentina.

trajectory.title: Won South American super flyweight title
trajectory.description: Defeated Vanesa Lorena Taborda on September 28, 2018 to capture the vacant South American super flyweight title with a unanimous decision.

trajectory.title: Won IBF junior flyweight world title
trajectory.description: Moved down two weight classes to defeat IBF champion Guadalupe Bautista by split decision on December 29, 2018, capturing her first world title.

trajectory.title: Added WBO light-flyweight title
trajectory.description: Stopped Venezuela's Debora Rengifo in the fifth round on March 26, 2022 to add the WBO female light-flyweight world title, becoming unified champion.

trajectory.title: Lost titles to Yokasta Valle
trajectory.description: Lost her unified titles via majority decision to Costa Rica's Yokasta Valle on November 26, 2022 in Carson, California.

trajectory.title: Regained IBF and WBO titles
trajectory.description: Defeated unbeaten Tania Enriquez by unanimous decision in March 2023 to regain her IBF and WBO light-flyweight titles.

trajectory.title: Unified WBA, IBF and WBO titles
trajectory.description: Stopped previously unbeaten Sara Bailey in the first round in Ottawa, Canada to win the WBA title and unify three major light-flyweight belts.

name: Carlos Isaías Morales Williams (Sech)
milestone_by_age_26: Released 'Otro Trago' in April 2019 at age 25, which hit #1 on Billboard's Hot Latin Songs chart, reached #34 on the US Billboard Hot 100, and was nominated for two Latin Grammy Awards; debut album 'Suenos' reached #3 on Billboard Top Latin Albums.
starting_point: Born December 3, 1993 in Rio Abajo, Panama City to parents who were both pastors; developed his singing voice in church choir and worked in food service and construction before music career.
current_position: Panamanian singer, songwriter, and record producer with three studio albums; continues releasing music under Rich Music and Rimas labels.

trajectory.title: Released first song with Los Principiantes
trajectory.description: Released 'Te Llamaba' with the group Los Principiantes in June 2008, beginning his musical career as a teenager.

trajectory.title: Released debut solo single
trajectory.description: Released his debut solo single 'Yo Sin Ti' in 2014, beginning his independent solo career while working day jobs in food service and construction.

trajectory.title: 'Miss Lonely' became national hit
trajectory.description: Released 'Miss Lonely' which went viral in Colombia and attracted the attention of producer DJ Dimelo Flow, leading to a deal with Rich Music.

trajectory.title: 'Otro Trago' hit #1 on Billboard Hot Latin Songs
trajectory.description: Released 'Otro Trago' in April 2019, which hit #1 on Billboard's Hot Latin Songs, reached #34 on the Billboard Hot 100, and was nominated for two Latin Grammy Awards.

trajectory.title: Released debut album Suenos
trajectory.description: Released debut studio album Suenos in April 2019, which reached #3 on Billboard Top Latin Albums and established Sech as a leading Latin R&B artist.

trajectory.title: Released second album 1 of 1
trajectory.description: Released his second studio album 1 of 1 on May 21, 2020, building on his breakthrough success with collaborations with major Latin artists.

trajectory.title: Released third album 42
trajectory.description: Released his third studio album 42 on April 15, 2022, exploring more up-tempo reggaeton while maintaining his signature R&B-inflected sound.

name: Enaldo Lopes de Oliveira Filho (Enaldinho)
milestone_by_age_26: Started YouTube channel in 2012, had viral breakthrough with '100 Camadas de Oreo' in 2016 at age 18 gaining 1M subscribers in two weeks (fastest-growing channel in the world), reached 10M subscribers by 2019, won Kids' Choice Award 2021, and had 35M+ subscribers by age 26 with R$25M+ annual revenue.
starting_point: Born March 26, 1998 in Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais, Brazil; father owned a cachaça factory; started YouTube channel for gaming videos in 2012.
current_position: Brazilian YouTuber and entrepreneur with 46.8 million YouTube subscribers, 24.7 billion views, and R$25 million+ annual revenue through licensing and media empire Elo.

trajectory.title: Created YouTube channel
trajectory.description: Created his YouTube channel on November 7, 2012, initially posting gaming videos of Combat Arms to share with friends.

trajectory.title: Pivoted to face-to-face content
trajectory.description: After attending a gaming fair and seeing how YouTubers were recognized, began appearing in videos with vlogs, pranks, and challenges targeting younger audiences.

trajectory.title: Viral breakthrough with 100 Camadas de Oreo
trajectory.description: The '100 Camadas de Oreo' video went viral, gaining 1 million subscribers in two weeks and making Enaldinho the fastest-growing channel in the world.

trajectory.title: Reached YouTube Diamond Play Button
trajectory.description: Surpassed 10 million YouTube subscribers, earning the Diamond Play Button and being named Best YouTuber of Latin America at the Streamy Awards.

trajectory.title: Won Kids' Choice Award
trajectory.description: Won the Kids' Choice Award and received a valuation offer of R$144 million for 49% of his company, which he declined.

trajectory.title: Named to Forbes Under 30 Brazil
trajectory.description: Featured in Forbes Under 30 Brazil with over 30 million followers and R$17 million in projected revenue from licensing and media.

trajectory.title: Reached R$25M annual revenue
trajectory.description: Grew his company Elo to R$25 million in annual revenue with over 100 licensed products, including clothing lines sold at C&A and collectible toys at Bob's.

name: Juan Pablo Martínez-Zurita Arellano (Juanpa Zurita)
milestone_by_age_26: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2016 at age 20, became one of Latin America's biggest digital creators with 51M+ combined followers by 2018, modeled for Calvin Klein, Louis Vuitton, and Dolce & Gabbana, raised 25M Mexican pesos for earthquake victims in 2017, and acted in Netflix's 'Luis Miguel' series by 2018.
starting_point: Born March 29, 1996 in Mexico City to Fernando Martinez-Zurita Reed, a political counselor, and Teresa Arellano; family moved to Washington D.C. during his youth; lives in Los Angeles.
current_position: Mexican internet personality, actor, and model with 31M+ combined followers; continues acting and content creation from Los Angeles.

trajectory.title: Posted first Vine video
trajectory.description: Posted his first Vine on June 11, 2013, titled 'That dog killed chuck norris and was after me,' featuring his dog Puca, receiving thousands of views.

trajectory.title: Named MTV Latin America Icon of the Year
trajectory.description: Chosen as 'icon of the year' by MTV Latin America, establishing himself as a leading digital creator in the Spanish-speaking world.

trajectory.title: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30
trajectory.description: Featured in Forbes 30 Under 30 as one of Latin America's biggest digital creators with over 31 million combined followers across platforms.

trajectory.title: Raised 25M pesos for earthquake victims
trajectory.description: Raised 25 million Mexican pesos through donations to build houses for victims of the September 2017 earthquake in Mexico City.

trajectory.title: Acted in Netflix's Luis Miguel series
trajectory.description: Played the role of Alex Basteri, Luis Miguel's brother, in the Netflix series Luis Miguel, marking his major acting debut.

trajectory.title: Released documentary Aislados
trajectory.description: Released a documentary titled Aislados in collaboration with Luisito Comunica in June 2020.

name: Druski
milestone_by_age_26: Amassed approximately 2.9 million Instagram followers by 2020 at age 25-26 through viral sketch comedy, with his 'Coulda Been Records' series gaining celebrity attention from Drake, Jack Harlow, and others.
starting_point: Born September 12, 1994 in Columbia, Maryland; grew up outside Atlanta, Georgia; attended Georgia Gwinnett College and Georgia Southern University before dropping out to pursue comedy.
current_position: Comedian, actor, and influencer with 12.2 million Instagram followers and 5.11 million YouTube subscribers; joined The Voice Season 29 as first-ever commentator; youngest BET Awards host in history.

trajectory.title: Started posting comedy skits on Instagram
trajectory.description: Began posting comedic skits on Instagram under the handle 'druski2funny' on October 2, 2017, playing characters including Kyle Rogger and a frat bro.

trajectory.title: Coulda Been Records series launched
trajectory.description: Created the 'Coulda Been Records' series, parodying a record label executive on Instagram Live, which caught the attention of Drake and other celebrities.

trajectory.title: Featured in major music videos
trajectory.description: Appeared in music videos for Lil Yachty's 'Oprah's Bank Account' and Drake's 'Laugh Now Cry Later' featuring Lil Durk in 2020.

trajectory.title: Opened for J. Cole and 21 Savage tour
trajectory.description: Joined The Off-Season tour as an opener for J. Cole and 21 Savage, transitioning from internet comedian to live performer.

trajectory.title: Coulda Fest sold out State Farm Arena
trajectory.description: Self-funded and sold out Coulda Fest, a 17,000-person comedy and music festival at State Farm Arena in Atlanta.

trajectory.title: Launched 4Lifers sports agency
trajectory.description: Launched his own sports agency, 4Lifers, with 2025 NFL draft prospect Princely Umanmielen as his first signee.

trajectory.title: Joined The Voice and hosted BET Awards
trajectory.description: Became the first-ever commentator on The Voice Season 29 and the youngest host in BET Awards history; named to TIME100 Creators list.

name: Marcello Hernández
milestone_by_age_26: Joined the cast of Saturday Night Live in 2022 at age 25, becoming the show's first Gen Z cast member, after being named a New Face of Comedy at Just for Laughs Montreal.
starting_point: Born August 19, 1997 in Miami, Florida to a Cuban mother and Dominican father; attended Belen Jesuit Preparatory School and graduated from John Carroll University in 2019.
current_position: SNL cast member in his fourth season; released Netflix comedy special American Boy in January 2025; starring in film 72 Hours with Kevin Hart.

trajectory.title: Started doing stand-up comedy
trajectory.description: Began performing stand-up at age 18, developing material inspired by his Cuban-Dominican immigrant upbringing in Miami.

trajectory.title: Graduated from John Carroll University
trajectory.description: Graduated with a degree in entrepreneurship and communication, having participated in the United States Hispanic Leadership Institute and Model UN.

trajectory.title: Named New Face of Comedy at Just for Laughs
trajectory.description: Selected as a New Face of Comedy at the prestigious Just for Laughs festival in Montreal, a key launching pad for emerging comedians.

trajectory.title: Joined Saturday Night Live cast
trajectory.description: Joined the cast of SNL for its 48th season in 2022, becoming the show's first Gen Z cast member.

trajectory.title: Hosted MLB Home Run Derby
trajectory.description: Hosted the 2024 MLB Home Run Derby, expanding his visibility beyond SNL into mainstream sports entertainment.

trajectory.title: Released Netflix special American Boy
trajectory.description: Released his hour-long Netflix comedy special American Boy in January 2025, marking a major career milestone.

trajectory.title: Starred in 72 Hours with Kevin Hart
trajectory.description: Shot a major supporting role alongside Kevin Hart in the Netflix film 72 Hours, set for release in July 2025.

name: Trevor Wallace
milestone_by_age_26: Created multiple viral comedy videos by 2019 at age 26, including the 'Kyle' meme video (May 2019) and the White Claw satire video (July 2019) that generated national media coverage and a cease-and-desist from the brand.
starting_point: Born December 30, 1992 in Camarillo, California; started comedy at 17 after his mother gave him an ad for a comedy class at Ventura Harbor Comedy Club; attended San Jose State University.
current_position: Comedian, writer, actor, and social media influencer with billions of views across platforms; released debut stand-up special Pterodactyl on Amazon Prime Video in 2023.

trajectory.title: Started comedy class
trajectory.description: Enrolled in a six-week comedy class at Ventura Harbor Comedy Club at age 17, falling in love with stand-up from the first class.

trajectory.title: First Vine video posted
trajectory.description: Published his first Vine video on April 24, 2013, while attending San Jose State University, beginning his social media comedy career.

trajectory.title: Moved to Los Angeles
trajectory.description: Moved to Los Angeles after university and began an internship with The Groundlings sketch comedy school and troupe.

trajectory.title: Zumiez videos went viral
trajectory.description: Posted a series of viral comedy videos about the brand Zumiez that received over 14 million views, establishing his social media presence.

trajectory.title: Kyle meme and White Claw videos went viral
trajectory.description: Created the 'Kyle' meme video in May 2019 and the White Claw satire in July 2019, with the latter generating a cease-and-desist from the brand.

trajectory.title: Started Stiff Socks podcast
trajectory.description: Began co-hosting the comedy podcast Stiff Socks with fellow comedian Michael Blaustein.

trajectory.title: Released debut stand-up special Pterodactyl
trajectory.description: Released his debut stand-up special Pterodactyl on Amazon Prime Video, performing at the Paramount Theatre in Austin, Texas.

name: Jaboukie Young-White
milestone_by_age_26: Co-wrote Netflix's 'American Vandal' and was hired as a correspondent on 'The Daily Show with Trevor Noah' in October 2018 at age 24, after making his television debut on 'The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon' in 2017.
starting_point: Born July 24, 1994 to Jamaican immigrants in Harvey, Illinois; attended Marian Catholic High School and DePaul University, leaving during his senior year in 2016 to pursue comedy full-time.
current_position: Comedian, actor, writer, and musician; known for voice roles in Strange World (2022) and Ruby Gillman, Teenage Kraken (2023); appeared in Companion (2025).

trajectory.title: First stand-up performance
trajectory.description: Performed stand-up for the first time at an open mic night at age 19, getting hired for his first stand-up gig at 21.

trajectory.title: Finalist at NYC Devil Cup Stand Up Festival
trajectory.description: Became a finalist at the 2016 NYC Devil Cup Stand Up Festival while performing at bars and clubs around Chicago and New York.

trajectory.title: TV debut on The Tonight Show
trajectory.description: Made his television debut as a guest performer on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, joking about racial stereotypes and coming out to his parents as gay.

trajectory.title: Co-wrote Netflix's American Vandal
trajectory.description: Co-wrote the Netflix mockumentary television series American Vandal and wrote for Big Mouth in 2018.

trajectory.title: Hired as Daily Show correspondent
trajectory.description: Joined The Daily Show with Trevor Noah as its Senior Youth Correspondent in October 2018, making his first appearance on October 11.

trajectory.title: First leading film role in Dating and New York
trajectory.description: Starred in his first leading role in the film Dating and New York, alongside supporting parts in Someone Great and C'mon C'mon.

trajectory.title: Voice role in Disney's Strange World
trajectory.description: Voiced a lead character in Disney's animated film Strange World, expanding his career into major studio animation.

name: Patti Harrison
milestone_by_age_26: Gained viral prominence in 2017 at age 26 for her appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, where she delivered a monologue about Trump's transgender military ban, becoming a breakout trans comedian.
starting_point: Born October 31, 1990 in Orient, Ohio to a Vietnamese mother and white American father who met during the Vietnam War; father died of a heart attack when she was six; youngest of seven children.
current_position: Actress and comedian known for Shrill, I Think You Should Leave, and Together Together; nominated for Independent Spirit Award for Best Female Lead.

trajectory.title: Moved to NYC for comedy career
trajectory.description: Moved to New York City to pursue comedy, participating in improv at Ohio University before dropping out and relocating.

trajectory.title: Viral Tonight Show appearance
trajectory.description: Gained wider prominence on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon with jokes about Trump's transgender military ban, becoming a breakout trans comedian.

trajectory.title: Hired as writer on Big Mouth
trajectory.description: Moved to Los Angeles and was hired as a writer on the Netflix animated series Big Mouth's third season.

trajectory.title: Cast in Hulu's Shrill
trajectory.description: Began playing Ruthie in the Hulu comedy series Shrill after co-star Aidy Bryant contacted her through Instagram and encouraged her to audition.

trajectory.title: Feature film debut in Together Together
trajectory.description: Made her feature film debut alongside Ed Helms in Together Together, earning an Independent Spirit Award nomination for Best Female Lead.

trajectory.title: First trans actor in Disney animated film
trajectory.description: Became the first known transgender actor to voice a character in a Disney animated film with Raya and the Last Dragon.

trajectory.title: Appeared in Theater Camp
trajectory.description: Appeared in the critically acclaimed comedy film Theater Camp, continuing her rise in film and television.

name: Matt Rife
milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest cast member in the history of MTV's 'Wild 'N Out' in 2015 at age 19, and appeared as a host on the reboot of TRL in 2017 at age 21.
starting_point: Born September 10, 1995 in Columbus, Ohio; raised in North Lewisburg, Ohio; first took interest in comedy at 14 after a teacher mentioned a high school talent show.
current_position: Comedian and actor with over 18 million TikTok followers and 7 million Instagram followers; released Netflix specials Natural Selection and Lucid; estimated $25M in earnings.

trajectory.title: Started performing stand-up professionally
trajectory.description: Began performing stand-up at age 15 at the Funny Bone in Columbus, Ohio, after encouragement from a friend to perform in a high school talent show.

trajectory.title: Youngest Wild 'N Out cast member
trajectory.description: Became the youngest cast member in the history of MTV's Wild 'N Out, a major break that introduced him to a national TV audience.

trajectory.title: Hosted TRL reboot
trajectory.description: Appeared as a host on the short-lived reboot of MTV's TRL and appeared on MTV's The Challenge: Champs vs. Stars.

trajectory.title: Featured on Bring the Funny
trajectory.description: Featured on NBC's comedy competition show Bring the Funny, advancing to the Semi-final Showcase before being eliminated in week 8.

trajectory.title: Self-produced first comedy special Only Fans
trajectory.description: Self-produced and distributed his first one-hour comedy special Only Fans on YouTube, marking his transition to full-time independent comedy.

trajectory.title: Released Netflix special Natural Selection
trajectory.description: Released his first Netflix comedy special Natural Selection, which became the streamer's most-watched comedy special of the year.

trajectory.title: Released Lucid on Netflix
trajectory.description: Released Lucid, Netflix's first crowd work comedy special, cementing his status as one of comedy's biggest touring acts.

name: Reneé Rapp
milestone_by_age_26: Made Broadway debut as Regina George in Mean Girls: The Musical on June 7, 2019 at age 19, after winning the 2018 Jimmy Awards for best high school musical theatre performance.
starting_point: Born January 10, 2000 to Charles Rapp and Denise Olexa in Huntersville, North Carolina; attended Hopewell High School before transferring to Northwest School of the Arts in Charlotte.
current_position: Singer-songwriter and actress; released second album Bite Me in August 2025; starred in Mean Girls 2024 film adaptation and The Sex Lives of College Girls on HBO Max.

trajectory.title: Won Jimmy Awards Best Performance
trajectory.description: Won the Jimmy Award for Best Performance by an Actress, beating competitors from across the country and catching the attention of Broadway producers.

trajectory.title: Cast as Wendla in Spring Awakening
trajectory.description: Was cast as Wendla in Theatre Charlotte's regional production of Spring Awakening, building her musical theater resume.

trajectory.title: Broadway debut as Regina George
trajectory.description: Made her Broadway debut as Regina George in Mean Girls: The Musical on June 7, 2019, initially for a limited run then permanently from September 10.

trajectory.title: Cast in The Sex Lives of College Girls
trajectory.description: Was cast as Leighton Murray, one of four leads in Mindy Kaling's HBO Max series The Sex Lives of College Girls.

trajectory.title: Released debut EP Everything to Everyone
trajectory.description: Released her debut EP Everything to Everyone, marking her transition from theater to pop music, followed by a deluxe edition in November.

trajectory.title: Released debut album Snow Angel
trajectory.description: Released her full-length studio album Snow Angel in 2023, realizing her long-held dream of becoming a pop star.

trajectory.title: Reprised Regina George in Mean Girls film
trajectory.description: Reprised her role as Regina George in the 2024 musical film adaptation of Mean Girls and contributed to its soundtrack.

trajectory.title: Released second album Bite Me
trajectory.description: Released her second studio album Bite Me on August 1, 2025, continuing her rise as a pop artist.

name: Tyrese Haliburton
milestone_by_age_26: Named an NBA All-Star in 2023 at age 23, becoming a 2x All-Star and 2x All-NBA selection, and led the Indiana Pacers to their first NBA Finals appearance in 25 years in 2025.
starting_point: Born February 29, 2000 in Oshkosh, Wisconsin; played college basketball at Iowa State before being drafted 12th overall by the Sacramento Kings in the 2020 NBA Draft.
current_position: NBA point guard for the Indiana Pacers; 2x All-Star and 2x All-NBA selection; led Pacers to 2025 NBA Finals; currently out for season with Achilles injury.

trajectory.title: Drafted 12th overall by Sacramento Kings
trajectory.description: Selected with the 12th pick by the Sacramento Kings in the 2020 NBA Draft and made his debut on December 23, 2020 against the Denver Nuggets.

trajectory.title: Named to NBA All-Rookie First Team
trajectory.description: Finished third in Rookie of the Year voting and was named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team after a strong debut season with Sacramento.

trajectory.title: Traded to Indiana Pacers
trajectory.description: Was traded to the Indiana Pacers on February 8, 2022 as part of a package for Domantas Sabonis, with the Pacers building around him as their centerpiece.

trajectory.title: Named NBA All-Star for first time
trajectory.description: Selected as a reserve for the Eastern Conference All-Star team, becoming the 15th Pacers player named an All-Star, averaging 20.7 points and 10.4 assists.

trajectory.title: Named All-Star starter and All-NBA
trajectory.description: Selected as an All-Star starter for the first time and named to the All-NBA Third Team, averaging 20.1 points and 10.9 assists per game.

trajectory.title: Led Pacers to NBA Finals
trajectory.description: Led the Indiana Pacers to their first NBA Finals appearance in 25 years, averaging 18.6 points and 9.2 assists in the regular season.

trajectory.title: Suffered season-ending Achilles injury
trajectory.description: Sustained an Achilles injury during the 2025-26 season, expected to return for the start of training camp the following season.

name: Zion Williamson
milestone_by_age_26: Selected 1st overall in the 2019 NBA Draft at 19 and became an NBA All-Star in 2021 at age 20, the fourth-youngest All-Star in NBA history.
starting_point: Born July 6, 2000 in Salisbury, North Carolina to parents who were both former college athletes; grew up in South Carolina and attended Spartanburg Day School, leading it to three consecutive state championships.
current_position: NBA power forward for the New Orleans Pelicans; 2x NBA All-Star; averaging 23.8 points and 6.4 rebounds for his career despite injury challenges.

trajectory.title: McDonald's All-American at Duke
trajectory.description: Named a McDonald's All-American and rated the No. 2 overall prospect in the class of 2018 by ESPN, committing to Duke University.

trajectory.title: National College Player of the Year at Duke
trajectory.description: Won every major National Player of the Year award as a freshman at Duke, averaging 22.6 points and 8.9 rebounds and leading Duke to an ACC Championship.

trajectory.title: Drafted 1st overall by New Orleans Pelicans
trajectory.description: Selected with the first overall pick in the 2019 NBA Draft by the New Orleans Pelicans on June 20, 2019.

trajectory.title: NBA debut and All-Rookie First Team
trajectory.description: Made his NBA debut on January 22, 2020, and was named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team after averaging 22.5 points per game.

trajectory.title: Named NBA All-Star
trajectory.description: Became the fourth-youngest NBA player selected to an All-Star game, averaging 27.0 points and 7.2 rebounds in his second season.

trajectory.title: Second NBA All-Star selection
trajectory.description: Named to his second NBA All-Star game, averaging 26.0 points and 7.0 rebounds in 29 games during the 2022-23 season.

trajectory.title: Continued NBA career with Pelicans
trajectory.description: Averaged 21.0 points and 5.7 rebounds in 62 games during the 2025-26 season, continuing to battle injuries throughout his career.

name: Cade Cunningham
milestone_by_age_26: Selected 1st overall in the 2021 NBA Draft at 20 and was named an NBA All-Star and All-NBA selection in 2025 at age 23.
starting_point: Born September 25, 2001 in Arlington, Texas; played quarterback in youth football which helped his passing; transferred to Montverde Academy in Florida where he was a consensus five-star recruit.
current_position: NBA point guard for the Detroit Pistons; 2x NBA All-Star and All-NBA selection; averaging 26.1 points and 9.1 assists in the 2024-25 season.

trajectory.title: Gold medal at FIBA U-19 World Cup
trajectory.description: Won a gold medal with the United States at the 2019 FIBA Under-19 World Cup, establishing himself on the international stage.

trajectory.title: Big 12 Player of the Year at Oklahoma State
trajectory.description: Named a consensus first-team All-American and Big 12 Player of the Year after his freshman season at Oklahoma State.

trajectory.title: Drafted 1st overall by Detroit Pistons
trajectory.description: Selected with the first overall pick in the 2021 NBA Draft by the Detroit Pistons on July 29, 2021.

trajectory.title: NBA debut and Rookie of the Year finalist
trajectory.description: Made his NBA debut on October 30, 2021, finishing third in Rookie of the Year voting after averaging 17.4 points and 5.6 assists.

trajectory.title: Season shortened by injury
trajectory.description: Played only 12 games in the 2022-23 season before requiring season-ending shin surgery, averaging 19.9 points and 6.0 assists.

trajectory.title: Named NBA All-Star and All-NBA
trajectory.description: Named an NBA All-Star and selected to the All-NBA Third Team after averaging 26.1 points and 9.1 assists in the 2024-25 season.

trajectory.title: Named All-NBA First Team
trajectory.description: Named to the All-NBA First Team and selected as an All-Star again, averaging 23.9 points and 9.9 assists in the 2025-26 season.

name: Evan Mobley
milestone_by_age_26: Selected 3rd overall in the 2021 NBA Draft at 20 and was named an NBA All-Star, All-NBA selection, and NBA Defensive Player of the Year in 2025 at age 23.
starting_point: Born June 18, 2001 in San Diego, California; father Eric Mobley was a former basketball player who coached Evan and his older brother Isaiah from an early age; attended Rancho Christian School in Temecula.
current_position: NBA power forward/center for the Cleveland Cavaliers; NBA All-Star, All-NBA Second Team, and Defensive Player of the Year; averaging 18.5 points and 9.3 rebounds.

trajectory.title: Pac-12 Player of the Year at USC
trajectory.description: Named Pac-12 Player of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year, and Freshman of the Year at USC, joining Anthony Davis as the only players from major conferences to win all three.

trajectory.title: Drafted 3rd overall by Cleveland Cavaliers
trajectory.description: Selected with the third overall pick in the 2021 NBA Draft by the Cleveland Cavaliers on July 29, 2021.

trajectory.title: NBA All-Rookie First Team
trajectory.description: Named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team after averaging 15.0 points and 8.3 rebounds, finishing second in Rookie of the Year voting.

trajectory.title: Named to NBA All-Defensive First Team
trajectory.description: Named to the NBA All-Defensive First Team and finished third in Defensive Player of the Year voting after averaging 16.2 points and 9.0 rebounds.

trajectory.title: NBA All-Star and Defensive Player of the Year
trajectory.description: Named an NBA All-Star for the first time, selected to All-NBA Second Team, and won the NBA Defensive Player of the Year award, averaging 18.5 points and 9.3 rebounds.

trajectory.title: Continued All-Star level play
trajectory.description: Averaged 18.2 points and 9.0 rebounds in 65 games during the 2025-26 season, maintaining his status as one of the NBA's elite two-way players.

name: Ansu Fati
milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest goalscorer in UEFA Champions League history at 17 years and 40 days in December 2019, having debuted for Barcelona at 16 and set multiple La Liga youngest-player records.
starting_point: Born October 31, 2002 in Bissau, Guinea-Bissau; moved to Seville at age five when his brother Braima signed for Sevilla; joined Barcelona's La Masia academy in 2012 at age ten.
current_position: Professional footballer on loan at Monaco from Barcelona; has represented the Spain national team; career impacted by injuries since 2020.

trajectory.title: Joined Barcelona's La Masia academy
trajectory.description: Joined FC Barcelona's youth academy La Masia in 2012 at age ten, a year after his brother had made the same move from Sevilla.

trajectory.title: First professional contract with Barcelona
trajectory.description: Signed his first professional contract with Barcelona on July 24, 2019, agreeing to a deal until 2022.

trajectory.title: La Liga debut for Barcelona
trajectory.description: Made his first team and La Liga debut on August 25, 2019, becoming the youngest ever person to play for Barcelona's first team in the league at 16 years and 298 days.

trajectory.title: Youngest Champions League goalscorer
trajectory.description: Became the youngest goalscorer in UEFA Champions League history at 17 years and 40 days in December 2019.

trajectory.title: Inherited Messi's number 10 shirt
trajectory.description: Was given Lionel Messi's iconic number 10 shirt after Messi's departure, symbolizing Barcelona's belief in Fati as their next star.

trajectory.title: Suffered career-altering knee injury
trajectory.description: Suffered a meniscus tear in November 2020 that required multiple surgeries, sidelining him for most of the 2020-21 season and impacting his trajectory.

trajectory.title: Loan to Brighton & Hove Albion
trajectory.description: Joined Brighton & Hove Albion on loan for the 2023-24 season to regain match fitness in the Premier League.

trajectory.title: Loan to Monaco
trajectory.description: Joined AS Monaco on loan for the 2025-26 season, continuing his journey to rediscover the form that made him a teenage phenomenon.

name: Scottie Barnes
milestone_by_age_26: Named NBA Rookie of the Year in 2022 at age 20 and became a 2x NBA All-Star (2024, 2026) with the Toronto Raptors.
starting_point: Born August 1, 2001 in West Palm Beach, Florida; attended Cardinal Newman High School before transferring to NSU University School and later Montverde Academy, where he was a consensus five-star recruit.
current_position: NBA forward for the Toronto Raptors; 2x NBA All-Star and All-Defensive Team selection; averaging 18.1 points and 7.5 rebounds in the 2025-26 season.

trajectory.title: ACC Rookie of the Year at Florida State
trajectory.description: Named the ACC conference rookie of the year and earned multiple honors in his freshman season at Florida State University.

trajectory.title: Drafted 4th overall by Toronto Raptors
trajectory.description: Selected with the fourth overall pick by the Toronto Raptors in the 2021 NBA Draft on July 29, 2021, a selection that surprised many analysts.

trajectory.title: Named NBA Rookie of the Year
trajectory.description: Won the NBA Rookie of the Year award after averaging 15.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, and 3.5 assists, beating out Evan Mobley and Cade Cunningham.

trajectory.title: First NBA All-Star selection
trajectory.description: Received his first All-Star selection after a breakout season averaging 19.9 points, 8.2 rebounds, and 6.0 assists, becoming the Raptors' franchise player.

trajectory.title: Signed rookie max extension
trajectory.description: Signed a rookie scale contract extension with the Toronto Raptors on July 8, 2024, cementing his role as the team's cornerstone.

trajectory.title: Second All-Star and All-Defensive Team
trajectory.description: Received his second All-Star selection and first All-Defensive Team honor, averaging 18.1 points and 7.5 rebounds while leading the Raptors back to competitiveness.

name: Alperen Sengun
milestone_by_age_26: Named Turkish Super League MVP at age 18 in 2021 while playing for Besiktas, then became an NBA All-Star in 2025 at age 22 with the Houston Rockets.
starting_point: Born July 25, 2002 in Giresun, Turkey; was also into swimming before concentrating on basketball; helped Turkey to a silver medal at the 2019 FIBA U-18 European Championships.
current_position: NBA center for the Houston Rockets; 2x NBA All-Star; averaging 20.4 points and 8.9 rebounds in the 2025-26 season.

trajectory.title: Silver medal at FIBA U-18 European Championships
trajectory.description: Helped Turkey to a silver medal at the 2019 FIBA Under-18 European Championships while earning All-Tournament Team honors.

trajectory.title: Turkish Super League MVP at Besiktas
trajectory.description: Named the Turkish Super League MVP while playing for Besiktas, establishing himself as one of Europe's top young prospects.

trajectory.title: Drafted 16th overall by Houston Rockets
trajectory.description: Selected with the 16th overall pick in the 2021 NBA Draft by Oklahoma City, then immediately traded to the Houston Rockets for two future first-round picks.

trajectory.title: NBA debut with Houston Rockets
trajectory.description: Made his NBA debut on October 20, 2021, recording 11 points and six rebounds, averaging 9.6 points and 5.5 rebounds in his rookie season.

trajectory.title: Breakout season averaging 21.1 points
trajectory.description: Averaged 21.1 points, 9.3 rebounds, and 5.0 assists in the 2023-24 season, becoming one of six players to average 20+ points, 9+ rebounds, and 5+ assists.

trajectory.title: Named NBA All-Star for first time
trajectory.description: Selected to his first NBA All-Star Game in the 2024-25 season, averaging 19.1 points and 10.3 rebounds for the Houston Rockets.

trajectory.title: Second consecutive All-Star selection
trajectory.description: Named to his second consecutive All-Star Game, averaging 20.4 points and 8.9 rebounds in the 2025-26 season.

name: Brooke Monk
milestone_by_age_26: Amassed 35M+ TikTok followers and was ranked #37 on Forbes Top Creators list in 2023 at age 20, with brand deals including Celsius and K18; signed with WME in 2022 at age 19.
starting_point: Born January 31, 2003 in Jacksonville, Florida; homeschooled her entire life; parents did not let her own a phone until age 16, just months before her TikTok fame began.
current_position: Content creator with over 72 million followers across platforms; estimated $2.6 million in annual earnings; resides in Los Angeles, California.

trajectory.title: Joined TikTok during COVID pandemic
trajectory.description: Downloaded TikTok in September 2019 at age 16 as a creative outlet while homeschooled, initially posting relatable content about school and relationships.

trajectory.title: Hit 1 million followers in two months
trajectory.description: Her following exploded rapidly, hitting 1 million followers within two months of starting, prompting her to update her parents about her viral growth.

trajectory.title: Graduated high school early to pursue content
trajectory.description: Graduated from high school early at 17 and chose to invest in her content creation career rather than attending college.

trajectory.title: Signed with WME talent agency
trajectory.description: Signed with WME talent agency in 2022, securing major brand deals and expanding her professional representation.

trajectory.title: Ranked #37 on Forbes Top Creators
trajectory.description: Ranked #37 on Forbes Top Creators list in 2023 with 35+ million TikTok followers and brand deals with Celsius, K18, and others.

trajectory.title: Reached 72 million followers across platforms
trajectory.description: Grew to over 72 million followers across platforms with an estimated $2.6 million in annual earnings, ranking among the biggest creators on the internet.

name: IShowSpeed (Darren Watkins Jr.)
milestone_by_age_26: Crossed 50 million YouTube subscribers on January 21, 2026, his 21st birthday, becoming the first Black creator to reach that milestone on the platform, during a livestream from Nigeria on his Africa tour, with 150M+ combined followers across platforms.
starting_point: Born January 21, 2005 in Cincinnati, Ohio; raised in the Bond Hill neighborhood; parents divorced when he was young; acquired the nickname 'Speedy' for his athleticism; great-grandson was Detroit's first African-American fire chief.
current_position: One of the world's most popular streamers with 57M+ YouTube subscribers, 53M TikTok followers, and 52M Instagram followers; performing at 2026 World Cup closing ceremony.

trajectory.title: Registered YouTube channel
trajectory.description: Registered his YouTube channel IShowSpeed in 2016 as a young teenager, initially posting gaming videos of NBA 2K and Fortnite with minimal viewership.

trajectory.title: Began regular livestreaming
trajectory.description: Started livestreaming regularly at age 15, broadcasting games like NBA 2K and Fortnite from his bedroom in Cincinnati.

trajectory.title: Viral breakthrough on TikTok
trajectory.description: Clips of his wild gaming outbursts went viral as memes on TikTok in 2021, dramatically growing his audience and establishing his chaotic streaming persona.

trajectory.title: Won Streamy Breakout Streamer award
trajectory.description: Won the 2022 Streamy Award for Breakout Streamer and began shifting focus toward general entertainment and soccer-related content centered on Cristiano Ronaldo.

trajectory.title: Won Streamy Variety Streamer award
trajectory.description: Won the 2023 Streamy Award for Variety Streamer and scored a viral goal at the Sidemen Charity Match.

trajectory.title: Met Cristiano Ronaldo and world tours
trajectory.description: Met his idol Cristiano Ronaldo live in Saudi Arabia in June 2024 and embarked on multi-continent IRL tours across the UK, Japan, Korea, India, and Brazil.

trajectory.title: Crossed 50M YouTube subscribers
trajectory.description: Became the first Black creator to reach 50 million YouTube subscribers on his 21st birthday during a livestream from Nigeria, with 150M+ combined followers.
